title: Emergency Agitation in T&A
brief_summary: Sevoflurane has been used commonly in pediatric anesthesia since 1990. However, it has caused more emergency agitation (EA) that other inhalation agents and the incidence is up to 80%. Therefore, lower minimum alveolar concentration of sevoflurane will reduce the EA when it is used with remifentanil in pediatric general anesthesia.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* American Society of Anesthesiologist physical status I or II
* 2-6 year-old children
* patients undergoing tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy

Exclusion Criteria:

* upper respiratory disease
* mental retardation
